name: opponent_prev_unsafe
description: Model 6 (paper Table 1): the probability of choosing Unsafe increases when the opponent chose Unsafe in the previous round (beta=0.607, SE=0.192, p=0.002).

name: progress_gap_before
description: Model 6: being further ahead (own progress minus opponent progress) reduces the probability of choosing Unsafe (beta=-0.296, SE=0.149, p=0.048).

name: first_round_unsafe
description: Model 6: choosing Unsafe in round 1 predicts later Unsafe play, significant only at the 10% level (beta=0.217, SE=0.116, p<0.10).

name: own_prev_unsafe
description: Model 6: the participant's own previous action is not a robust predictor once the opponent's previous action and race state are included (beta=-0.193, SE=0.192, not significant). This is a null replication and must be scored by TOST equivalence to zero, not by failing to reject.

name: contrast_0.6_vs_0.9
description: Pre-registered 0.6-vs-0.9 contrast on participant-level mean Unsafe frequency: negligible observed effect (Cohen's d=-0.027, t=-0.206, p=0.837, Table S3). This is a null replication and must be scored by equivalence, not by failing to reject.

name: contrast_0.1_vs_0.6
description: 0.1-vs-0.6 contrast on participant-level mean Unsafe frequency (Table S3): Cohen's d=0.341, i.e. Unsafe is HIGHER at the low-risk treatment. Taken from the table value, not the Figure 2A caption, which states the opposite direction.

name: phi_U_overall
description: Overall mean Unsafe frequency (phi_U) across all treatments and rounds (Table S3): 0.584.

name: share_AS
description: Always Safe is never a Nash equilibrium of the reduced four-strategy game at any studied maximum private risk (paper Results/SI) and is not reported as a materially used strategy. No exact participant-level share is given in the main text, so this is a qualitative near-absence anchor rather than a precise observed frequency.
